TUT.title: The refund message
TUT.brief: Riya has brought a fictional phone to the kiosk. Inspect the conversations, identify the pressure tactics, and rebuild what happened. No real money is used.
TUT.closing: Case closed. You checked the evidence, named the tactics, and chose a safer response.
TUT.debrief.mechanism: The sender creates a story, adds pressure, discourages outside checks, and asks for money or account access.
TUT.debrief.c1: Pause before responding to a message that creates pressure.
TUT.debrief.c2: Verify the claim through a contact you find independently.
TUT.debrief.c3: Protect your payment details and ask a trusted person for help.
TUT-E01: A message says: I am from your bank support desk. Use this private chat for your refund.
TUT-01.explain: A name in a message does not prove who sent it. Contact the bank through its own app.
TUT-L1.q: Which detail in the phone shows a claimed identity?
TUT-L1.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
TUT-E02: Your refund expires in ten minutes. Reply now.
TUT-02.explain: The countdown discourages checking. A pause gives you time to verify.
TUT-L2.q: Which detail in the phone shows time pressure?
TUT-L2.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
TUT-E03: Send your payment PIN here to receive the refund.
TUT-03.explain: A request for a secret payment PIN is a request for account access. Never share it.
TUT-L3.q: Which detail in the phone shows a request for money or access?
TUT-L3.nudge: Look at the sender’s request. Tap the sentence and select the tactic it demonstrates.
TUT-H1: The message uses a colourful banner.
TUT-H1.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.
TUT-H2: The message uses a smiley face.
TUT-H2.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.
TUT-H3: The message uses capital letters in the greeting.
TUT-H3.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.
TUT-O01: Library group: The reading room opens at nine tomorrow.
TUT-O02: Mum: Dinner is on the table.
TUT-O03: Sports club: Practice starts at four.
TUT-O04: Bookshop: The novel you ordered has arrived.
TUT.fix.q: What is the safest next step?
TUT.fix.safe: Stop the conversation, verify independently, and ask a trusted person for help.
TUT.fix.safe.why: This removes the pressure and gives you a reliable way to check the request.
TUT.fix.pay: Send the money first and check later.
TUT.fix.pay.why: Sending money first gives the sender what they want before the claim is verified.
TUT.fix.share: Share the requested account details to settle the matter.
TUT.fix.share.why: Account secrets and device access should stay private, regardless of the story.
TUT.replay.1: The sender starts a story to attract attention.
TUT.replay.2: A claimed identity or frightening statement makes the story feel important.
TUT.replay.3: The sender asks for money, secrets, or control of the device.
